text: dsh-read-url 是为 DSH 提供网页与在线内容阅读能力的插件，通过四个工具接入：读取单页正文、列出页面链接、并行读取多条 URL，以及从入口页遍历同站页面。读取时可提取 HTML 主体并转成精简文本或结构化 Markdown，也可处理 JSON、纯文本、CSV 与 RSS/Atom；支持常见字符集识别、分页拼接、链接和元数据输出，以及带缓存的 offset 续读。适合需要在 DSH 会话中阅读网页、文档、数据 API 或订阅源的用户。无需 API key；核心运行时使用 Node.js 20 及内置能力，SPA 渲染可选安装 Playwright 与 Chromium。

dsh-read-url reads pages, lists links, batches URLs, and crawls sites through four DSH tools. It extracts HTML as text or Markdown and handles JSON, text, CSV, and RSS/Atom, with charset detection, pagination, continuation, and optional SPA rendering. No API key; requires Node.js 20.
我想把一篇网页文章交给 DSH 阅读并提炼重点。
能不能把网页正文清理出来，别把导航栏也带进来？
我有一篇很长的文章，想分段续读而且不要重复抓取。
帮我同时读几条网页链接，方便比较不同来源。
我想查看某个网站有哪些页面和链接结构。
DSH 能直接整理 RSS、Atom 或 JSON API 的内容吗？
I want DSH to extract the readable article text from a URL.
Can I compare several web pages by reading them in one parallel request?
I need a compact map of pages linked from one site entry point.
dsh-read-url 的功能「读取网页正文」：调用 read_url 并传入 URL，可选择纯文本或 Markdown、返回字符上限和续读 offset；结果包括标题、正文与可选链接。
dsh-read-url 的功能「读取多种内容格式」：读取 HTML、JSON、纯文本、Markdown、CSV 和 RSS/Atom，按内容类型提取并整理成适合模型阅读的紧凑结果。
dsh-read-url 的功能「列出页面链接」：调用 read_url_links 并提供 URL，可设置返回数量；工具返回链接文字和解析后的 HTTP(S) 地址，不附带正文。
dsh-read-url 的功能「并行批量阅读」：调用 read_url_batch 输入多条 URL，可选择 Markdown 或文本并设置每页长度；每页独立返回结果，单页失败不会中断整批。
dsh-read-url 的功能「站点页面遍历」：调用 read_url_site 输入入口 URL，可设置页数、深度和是否附短摘要；按同一主机遍历页面并返回标题、层级和长度。
dsh-read-url 的功能「分页文章拼接」：读取带有明确下一页标记的同站文章时，自动跟进有限页数并合并正文，避免重复段落；可通过配置调整分页开关和页数上限。
dsh-read-url 的功能「长正文续读」：首次读取后可设置 offset 继续取回缓存中的后续字符，返回字符位置和总长度信息，帮助分段查看长文。
dsh-read-url 的功能「可选 SPA 页面渲染」：正文静态提取为空或很短且页面包含脚本时，可用已安装的 Playwright 与 Chromium 渲染页面后再提取内容。
dsh-read-url 使用前须知：JavaScript 驱动页面的浏览器渲染不是核心依赖；要启用该增强，需要在 DSH profile 中安装 Playwright 和 Chromium。
dsh-read-url 使用前须知：通过 DSH web provider 读取时，提供方可能只返回已解码文本，因此 HTML 链接扫描、元数据和分页行为取决于提供方给出的内容类型。

URL reader plugin for DeepSeek Harness: fetch any URL — **webpages (HTML), JSON APIs, RSS/Atom feeds** — auto-detect encoding (UTF-16 BOM / GBK/GB2312 / UTF-8 / Big5 / Shift-JIS), extract the clean main content (**auto-joining paginated articles**), and return **token-efficient compact text or structured Markdown**.
dsh-read-url README · dsh-read-url：Zero runtime dependencies (Node 20+ built-ins handle fetch/decode/extract), no API key, no server side — install and use.

dsh-read-url README · Supported content：- HTML technical documentation, forums, nested articles and custom elements, with visible code examples and metadata preserved.
- Plain text, Markdown, CSV, JSON and vendor `+json` APIs.
- RSS 1.0/2.0 and Atom, including namespace prefixes, relative article links and `xml:base`.
- UTF-16 BOM text without a Content-Type header.

dsh-read-url README · Supported content：Continue at `charsStart + charsReturned`; the returned `charsStart` may exceed the requested offset when paragraph separators are skipped. Markdown tables convert at most the first 25 rows and report omitted rows.

dsh-read-url README · Why：This plugin keeps URL-reading output compact: **cleaned body + essential metadata** from HTML, paragraph-aligned truncation, continuation and a session cache. It also preserves plain text or Markdown returned by the configured DSH provider. DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 includes a DeepSeek Fetch API provider, so available source content and metadata depend on the selected provider.

dsh-read-url README · Competitor comparison (measured from source/docs, 2026-08-15)：> Measured 2026-08-16 (local environment): with this plugin removed, the official `web_fetch` hitting `https://www.baidu.com` had its TLS handshake intercepted by a middlebox using program fingerprints (fell back to http to succeed), and Baidu returned a **server-side degraded page** (trending topics moved to JS loading, absent from static HTML). With `dsh-read-url` restored, https worked and trending topics were fully readable. Root cause: the request's UA and TLS characteristics decide whether sites/middleboxes treat you as a bot.

dsh-read-url README · Usage：Just talk to the agent:

```
Read https://example.com/article and summarize the key points
Read https://docs.example.org/guide in markdown mode

dsh-read-url README · Real examples (measured)：**1. Token economy — return only what the model needs**

`read_url` on a portal returns cleaned body capped at `maxChars` (default 6,000) — not the raw page with nav/ads/footers. Repeat reads hit the 5-min cache (`(cached)`), so the agent never re-fetches:

```
title: 新闻中心首页_新浪网
charset utf-8
(chars 800/12398 — 截断，offset 续读)
```

**2. Overseas sites — direct + proxy race**

dsh-read-url README · Real examples (measured)：When a proxy is configured, the direct fetch and the proxy `curl` start together and the first to complete wins. A blocked overseas site that used to cost ~11s (direct-connect timeout + fallback) now reads in under a second:

```
BBC 中文: OK (633ms) — clean 4,000+ chars of headline news
```

**3. Long-article continuation (`offset`)**

A 12,000-char article is read in slices; `offset` resumes from cache without repeating earlier text — the model keeps exactly what it needs in context:

dsh-read-url README · Real examples (measured)：```
chars 800+800/12398 · cached
```

**4. Batch research across pages**

`read_url_batch` reads up to 10 pages in parallel (concurrency 4), each cleaned individually, failures isolated:

```
读取 2/4 页成功，2 页失败
--- 阮一峰的网络日志 (491 字符) ---
--- Example Domain (127 字符) ---
[失败] https://zh.wikipedia.org/... — Fetch failed: HTTP 403 ...

dsh-read-url README · Tools：**`read_url(url, maxChars?, offset?, mode?, includeLinks?)`** — fetch and extract clean body. Handles HTML pages, JSON APIs (fully compact render with long-value clipping) and RSS/Atom feeds (entry list + `feedCount`); paginated articles (novel/news/forum) are auto-joined up to `paginateMax` pages; page metadata (`published`, `author`) is harvested automatically — **meta → schema.org JSON-LD → byline, three-tier fallback** (v1.3.0: JSON-LD fills publication time/author on news sites); `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` shell pages (link hops / anti-hotlink relays / no-JS SPA entries) are followed to the real page automatically (≤3 hops, loop-safe, fails open on fetch errors, v1.3.0); pages declaring `<base href>` (frame sites / legacy forums) resolve relative links against it (v1.3.0)

|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | required | http(s) URL |
| `maxChars` | number | 6000 | Max body characters returned (500–20000) |
| `offset` | number | 0 | Resume reading from this character offset (long-article continuation; served from cache without repeating earlier text) |
| `mode` | string | `text` | `text` = plain (most token-efficient); `markdown` = structured |
| `includeLinks` | boolean | `false` | Also return up to 20 page links (title+URL) |

dsh-read-url README · Configuration (optional)：Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (defaults in the plugin's own `cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: dsh-read-url
  config:
    timeoutMs: 15000      # per-request timeout (500-120000, clamped)
    maxBytes: 3145728     # response body cap (bytes)

Values are coerced and clamped to sane ranges at load — quoted numbers in YAML work, garbage falls back to defaults.

dsh-read-url README · Explicit direct origins (v1.9.0)：`directFetchOrigins` defaults to `[]`. For a trusted local reverse proxy (for example, a GitHub hostname mapped by your hosts file), explicitly list the origins in the plugin's **profile configuration**, then reload the plugin/profile:

```yaml
- id: dsh-read-url
  config:
    directFetchOrigins:
      - https://github.com

dsh-read-url README · Explicit direct origins (v1.9.0)：Listed origins use direct fetch immediately, bypassing the host web provider **and its SSRF checks**. Add only origins you trust; this also permits their DNS/hosts mappings to local or private addresses. The option is not a tool argument. Unlisted initial URLs keep the existing provider selection and fallback behavior; a provider refusal does not enable this exception automatically.

dsh-read-url README · Explicit direct origins (v1.9.0)：Matching is exact after URL normalization: scheme, hostname and port must match; subdomains are separate. At most 32 entries of 2,048 characters each are accepted. Only an HTTP(S) origin with an optional trailing `/` is valid: credentials, paths, queries, fragments, wildcards and ambiguous syntax cause a configuration error. Unlike numeric options, invalid entries do not fall back to defaults.

dsh-read-url README · Explicit direct origins (v1.9.0)：Once a request selects explicit direct retrieval, every subsequent HTTP redirect, meta-refresh, pagination request and descendant crawl stays within the list. Redirects handled internally by the provider remain on the provider path. Direct HTTP requests follow at most 5 redirects per attempt and stop loops early. An outside target is stopped before requesting it; refresh/pagination blocked by this policy retain the readable static result with a hint. Explicit direct reads use neither the plugin's curl proxy race nor SPA rendering, preventing those mechanisms from widening the exception. When `spaRender` is enabled and `read_url` or `read_url_links` would otherwise render a script-only page, they return a static-reading hint. Cancellation, response-size limits and one bounded Retry-After retry still apply. All four tools share the policy; success and failure caches are isolated by the complete normalized list, including after changing or clearing it.

dsh-read-url README · Explicit direct origins (v1.9.0)：Controlled HTTP servers and provider fixtures cover default refusals, explicit routing, redirects, pagination, all four tools, cache isolation, cancellation, timeouts and response-size limits.

- Local maintenance validation (2026-09-07): **102 OK / 27 THIN+EMPTY / 23 ERR / 0 THREW** across 152 sites, with no noise among OK results; 53 adversarial probes pass. ERR results are network/anti-bot failures, invalid addresses or intentionally unsupported binary types. Known NOISE flags were checked against the previous code using identical inputs.
- Real case: on a Xiaoheihe post, comment like-counts (`up` field) could not be attributed from flattened text — **precise fields should come from the page's underlying data API** (e.g. `/bbs/app/link/tree` JSON). This is a shared boundary of text extractors, not a defect.
